summary: The narrator, who is recovering after a clinic visit, is told by a doctor with holistic methods that they are virtually certain of something and that continuing the program is their own decision. They decide to collect their things and leave, the doctor says their clothes are in a room with a closet, and they confirm insurance coverage is free. In the dark room, a childlike young woman with braided hair and red glass beads gives them a baggie of plastic vials of gray and green herbal powders, telling them they are special and that they are near 'them.' The narrator declines to take the herbs and starts to dress, growing wary and puzzled about the clinic and its purpose.
one_line: A narrator leaving a strange holistic clinic is pressed by a braided young woman to take mysterious herbal powders.
key_facts: The narrator had mixed feelings about the doctor's 'holistic' medicine.
The doctor said he was 'virtually certain' about something and that continuing the program was the narrator's own decision.
The narrator said they would talk more about the program when feeling better.
The doctor said the narrator's clothes were in their room, in a closet in the corner by the window.
When asked whether Blue Cross covered the treatment, the doctor replied 'On the house.'
The narrator noticed a large white door that appeared to lead to another wing of the clinic.
The room was dark when the narrator returned, and the shuffling sound was someone closing the Venetian blinds.
A short woman, childlike but probably mid-twenties, had dark hair done in multiple braids with a red glass bead at the end of each.
The woman said, 'You're special. We all know it. That's why he brought you over here, to this building. To be near them.'
The woman carried a fanny pack and took out a baggie filled with plastic vials of herbs she said she had started growing there.
The herbs were clear plastic medicine bottles containing various gray and green powders and flakes.
The woman instructed the narrator to put two teaspoons of each herb in boiled water and drink it every day for a week.
The narrator set the herbs aside and said, 'I'm going to be just fine, really.'
